sourceExcerpt:
Ana Ivanovic’s First Roland-Garros Title

Ana Ivanovic secured her maiden Grand Slam victory on June 7, 2008, at Roland-Garros by defeating Dinara Safina 6-4, 6-3 in the women’s final. The match, held on the iconic Philippe-Chatrier Court in Paris, showcased Ivanovic’s aggressive baseline game and mental resilience. She lost just one set throughout the tournament, in a high-stakes semifinal against fellow Serbian Jelena Jankovic, which determined the new world No. 1.

Justine Henin, who had dominated the French Open with three consecutive titles before retiring, handed the silver trophy to the 20-year-old from Belgrade. This victory made Ivanovic the first Serbian player to claim a major singles championship. Off the court, her modeling career and popular personal website further elevated her profile, cementing her status as one of tennis’s rising stars.

Muguruza’s Breakthrough at Roland Garros

Spain’s Garbiñe Muguruza claimed her first major trophy on June 4, 2016, at the French Open in Paris by defeating defending champion Serena Williams 7-5, 6-4. Under cloudy skies at Roland Garros, Muguruza used powerful groundstrokes and aggressive court positioning to break Williams’ serve four times, overcoming nine double faults to maintain control of the match.

Williams, seeking a record-tying 22nd Grand Slam, finished with 39 forced errors compared to Muguruza’s 21. On match point, Muguruza executed a perfectly placed lob that landed on the baseline, prompting applause from Williams and sending the Spaniard into an emotional collapse on the clay. Muguruza then rose to kiss the silver trophy, cementing a landmark victory in her tennis career.

Krejcikova’s Roland Garros Triumph

Barbora Krejcikova sealed her first Grand Slam singles title at the 2021 French Open with a 6-1, 2-6, 6-4 victory over Anastasia Pavlyuchenkova. On the red clay of Roland Garros, Krejcikova displayed remarkable composure and tactical variety, recovering from a second-set loss to clinch the final set and lift the Coupe Suzanne-Lenglen.

Dressed in a navy jacket and white visor, Krejcikova kissed the silver trophy presented by Martina Navratilova, becoming the first Czech woman since 1981 to win the Paris singles crown. Her win also marked her entry into the WTA Top 20 at world No.15 and extended her unbeaten run to 12 matches. This victory followed her earlier doubles success at Roland Garros and underscored her rapid rise in singles competition.

Mirra Andreeva’s Triumph at Roland‑Garros 2026

Mirra Andreeva, the 19-year-old rising star and Rolex testimonee, clinched her first Grand Slam title at the 2026 French Open. In a decisive 1 hour 22 minute final on the red clay of Court Philippe‑Chatrier, she overcame her opponent to lift the prestigious Suzanne‑Lenglen Trophy. The silver cup, engraved with “CHAMPIONNATS INTERNATIONAUX DE FRANCE SIMPLE DAMES COUPE SUZANNE LENGLEN,” gleams as Andreeva kisses it in celebration, wearing a pink visor and black jacket.

This victory places Andreeva among a select group of teenage champions at Roland‑Garros, joining the ranks of Björn Borg, Chris Evert, and Iga Świątek. The tournament’s challenging conditions—scorching heat and demanding matches—provided a stage for the next generation of tennis stars. Rolex’s decades-long partnership with the French Open, which began in 2019, is underscored by this moment, as the brand continues to support champions who redefine excellence on clay.
